facts.title: The world’s most watched portrait
facts.body: Leonardo’s Mona Lisa (begun c. 1503) is almost certainly Lisa Gherardini, wife of Francesco del Giocondo. The Louvre’s panel is famous for sfumato, an invented landscape, and a smile that refuses to settle.

facts.title: Lisa Gherardini
facts.body: Documentary and stylistic evidence identify the sitter as Lisa Gherardini. Leonardo kept the panel with him for years, refining it beyond a simple commission.

facts.title: A smile that moves
facts.body: Peripheral vision softens the mouth; direct stare hardens it. Leonardo engineered ambiguity into the face itself.

facts.title: Hands as quiet architecture
facts.body: The folded hands close the lower pyramid of the composition — calm, deliberate, unfinished by jewelry.

facts.title: Veil like mist
facts.body: A translucent veil over hair and bodice continues Leonardo’s obsession with light through thin matter.

facts.title: A world behind her
facts.body: The background is not a real Tuscan view but an aerial fantasy of roads, water, and rock — weather and geology as mood.

facts.title: A bridge at mid-distance
facts.body: A small arched bridge pins the right middle ground, giving scale to an otherwise dreamlike terrain.

facts.title: The chair’s edge
facts.body: A chair arm at left reminds us she sits in a room — then the room dissolves into landscape.

facts.title: Sfumato — smoke without lines
facts.body: Leonardo dissolves contours into tone. Eyes, lips, and jaw live in soft transitions rather than hard outlines.
